guidance.procedure: Evaluate breadth, identification, and communication form independently from the complete operative definition. Technical-only coverage requires an exclusively technical protected class; do not infer breadth from a title, recital, purpose clause, or isolated example. Express inclusion of business, financial, commercial, or other non-technical material opposes technical-only coverage. Explicit identification requires a universal marking or designation condition; coverage regardless of labeling opposes it. For oral or visual information, preserve contemporaneous designation and any later written-confirmation condition. Cite every operative fragment completing the definition or condition, including independently responsive repeated provisions, but exclude headings, party descriptions, exclusions answering another proposition, and merely adjacent text.

Run three separate lifecycle tests. For return or destruction, match the stated trigger exactly: termination or expiration supports a termination-triggered duty, while request, demand, or the end of discussions alone does not. For retention, inspect the disposition command and all express archival, backup, legal-record, or dispute exceptions; an all-information-and-copies command without such an exception supports the opposed boundary. For survival, require obligations expressly continuing after termination, rather than a fixed term, antecedent-breach liability, or a disposition clause. Cite the trigger, disposition scope, responsive exception, and continuation language only; do not borrow evidence between the three tests.

Match the receiving actor, disclosure or copying action, recipient class, quantifier, and condition separately. For employee sharing, cite only clauses governing employees and every fragment carrying need-to-know, authorization, or confidentiality conditions. For third-party sharing, separately inspect consultants, advisers, contractors, affiliates, agents, and other outsiders; an employee-only authorization plus an outsider prohibition supports the restrictive boundary. Discretionary written consent is not a standing permission. For copying, distinguish an absolute or consent-only prohibition from a necessity- or purpose-limited operative exception. Include independently responsive repeated rules, but exclude safeguards, recipient-liability clauses, use restrictions, headings, and neighboring recipient classes.

Trace each exception from the operative exclusion or permission lead-in through the responsive subparagraph. Independent development must concern development without use of, reference to, or access to protected information. Third-party acquisition requires an external source entitled to disclose and, where stated, free of a confidentiality duty; public-domain, prior-possession, and employee-access provisions are not substitutes. Treat compelled disclosure permission and notice as separate propositions: verify legal compulsion, the notice requirement or express excuse, protective-order opportunity, and any required-portion limit. Cite the lead-in whenever it supplies exclusion scope and every continuation needed for the responsive exception, but exclude neighboring exceptions and headings.

For each proposition, first match the regulated actor, direct conduct, object, people covered, modality, duration, and exceptions. Reverse engineering requires express reverse-engineer, decompile, disassemble, decrypt, decipher, reconstruct, test, or materially equivalent conduct directed at protected material or an embodying product; definitions, confidentiality, copying, ownership, severability, and limited-use clauses are not substitutes. Solicitation requires recruiting, soliciting, inducing departure, hiring, engagement, or comparable conduct directed at the specified people. Cite all fragments completing the actor and restriction, but no unrelated confidentiality or remedy text.

Test rights and agreement secrecy separately. No-license requires operative language that no license, right, title, interest, option, or other right is granted or implied; ownership, restricted use, access, or a disclaimer alone is insufficient. Agreement confidentiality requires protection of the agreement's existence or terms, or of the fact, status, or substance of negotiations or discussions; an entire-agreement clause or ordinary confidentiality of disclosed information is not responsive. Cite every fragment carrying the protected subject and prohibition, excluding headings, signatures, purpose clauses, and neighboring ownership or use text.

Find every independently operative restriction limiting use of protected information to the agreement's stated purpose. Match the regulated actor, protected object, allowed purpose, and any clause that defines or independently restates that purpose. A disclosure rule, confidentiality duty, ownership clause, copy restriction, recital, or permission to receive information is not itself a use limitation. Cite all responsive repeated operative provisions, even when one is already sufficient, while excluding headings, recipient-class clauses, and adjacent restrictions that merely help interpretation.

For oral or visual information, preserve contemporaneous designation and later written-confirmation requirements. Cite the complete grammatical chain and independently operative repeated definitions; exclude titles, recitals, exclusions, and neighboring categories that do not supply scope.

(i) technologies in written or tangible form disclosed to COMPANY from time to time after the Effective Date of this Agreement by ROCHESTER and identified with particularity at time of disclosure and marked confidential; and
